idea: Battery and solar cost curve tracking service
pain: Cost curves drive every transition investment case and public data lags badly
v1: A quarterly cost curve update with China-sourced inputs
verdict: Compounding data asset with real China-sourced advantage; slow to establish credibility.

why.distribution: Warm fund contacts on the demand side.
why.demand: BNEF and Wood Mackenzie are paid handsomely for this - a strong paid substitute exists.
why.fmf: Her analysis skill plus China sourcing; she is not a technology specialist.
why.revenue_structure: Annual data subscription, very sticky once embedded.
why.defensibility: A proprietary time series with primary Chinese inputs compounds and cannot be back-filled.
why.time_to_revenue: Credibility requires several quarters of history: 6-9 months.
why.tailwind: Central to every transition investment case.
why.ceiling: £1,200/mo x 14 subscribers = £202k, against very well-funded incumbents.

ceiling_arithmetic: £1,200/mo x 14 subscribers = £202k less ~£20k sourcing = £182k. The incumbents charge far more but are trusted; winning 14 subscribers means displacing or supplementing BNEF. Realistic: 4-6 = £58-86k.
carries: A compounding proprietary dataset with a sourcing advantage incumbents lack.
kills: Time to revenue and incumbent strength. BNEF and Wood Mackenzie are entrenched and well resourced.
test: Ask four energy funds what they pay BNEF and what it misses.
test_pass: They name a China-sourcing gap worth paying for.
test_fail: They are satisfied with existing providers.
